02

Housekeeping

We want you on the right trip and having the best week possible. So here's what the brochures leave out.

  • Every class is optional. This is your vacation. Skip a morning, sleep in, go to the beach. Nobody's taking attendance.
  • First time on a reformer, or new to yoga? Let us know. We're happy to walk you through the basics during free time, or whenever works for you. Every class is all levels, with options for every body.
  • Amorgos has no airport. You'll fly into Athens, Santorini, Mykonos, Naxos or Paros, then take a ferry. It's part of why the island feels so untouched. Build in buffer and it's easy.
  • Greece runs on Greek time. Ferries run late, dinner tends to have a loose start time and "5 minutes" is a feeling. Hold the schedule loosely.
  • May is warm, not hot. Sunny days around 22°C / 72°F, cooler breezy evenings. The sea is refreshing (read: cold at first), around 18°C / 64°F.
  • You're sharing space with people you may not know. Many people come solo, some come with friends. By day 3 it won't feel that way. If something or someone is bothering you, tell us early (see our Anonymous Feedback Form in What to Expect). We can fix things in real time. Don't wait until the week is over to put it out there. That's a disservice to you and to the people around you.
  • Plans can change. Weather, boats, and local life sometimes rearrange the itinerary. Of course we'll try to stick to the itinerary as laid out. If we need to adapt, we'll swap in something just as good and tell you right away. We ask that you stay flexible and patient with the situation.

06

Getting there + getting home

You book your own flights and ferries, so you can come from anywhere and add travel on either side. Booking your own doesn't mean you're on your own. Send us any flight or ferry before you book if you want our eyes on it.

The only two times you need
ARRIVE
Get a ferry that lands on Amorgos (Katapola or Aegiali port) between 1pm and 4pm on Monday, May 10.
DEPART
Take whichever ferry works best for you, any time from noon onward on Saturday, May 15.

Arriving earlier than 1pm? Totally fine, but your room may not be ready until check-in. The hotel will hold your bags, and the pool and spa are yours in the meantime.

Lots of flight options. We know there are a ton of different ways to get to Greece. If you're looking at flights that don't line up with these time frames, send them to us and we'll help you coordinate.

MAKE A WEEKEND OF IT

We highly encourage you to use the weekend before the retreat to see another Greek island. Santorini, Mykonos, Naxos, Paros, take your pick. They're all a ferry ride from Amorgos, so you can island-hop Saturday and Sunday and sail over Monday afternoon. Want ideas for where to go or stay? Email us. We love this stuff.

Amorgos has no airport, so you'll fly into another city in Greece and take a ferry to the island. How you get to the port is up to you.

Group transfers: We arrange transfers from both ports to Aegialis on Monday afternoon, and back to the port on Saturday. You'll be grouped with others arriving around the same time, so you may wait a little for the rest of your ferry crew. We'll put everyone on the same ferry into a small group chat the week before so you can find each other. Look for the driver holding an Aegialis sign.

Arriving or leaving outside these times? No problem. Just let us know and we'll help you arrange your own transfer (the hotel can book cars).

Your ferry options

In May you can reach Amorgos by direct ferry or high-speed boat from Athens, Santorini, Mykonos, Naxos and Paros, all with airports that connect to major cities. Amorgos has two ports, Katapola and Aegiali. Which one you land at depends on your boat, and we pick you up at either.

Our pick: SeaJets. They're the high-speed boats, and they run the Santorini and Mykonos routes. The easiest route is flying in and out of Santorini. The SeaJet to Katapola takes about 1 to 1.5 hours.

Plan around the new border checks

Europe now takes your fingerprints and photo at your first Schengen airport (the EES system). Lines can be long at peak. Full details are in Passports + Entry, but for booking flights:

  • Clear passport control at a big hub (Athens, Frankfurt, Paris, Amsterdam, Munich), not at Santorini or Mykonos airport, where lines are worst.
  • Leave 2+ hours for any connection after your first landing in Europe.
  • Arrive by Sunday, May 9. No same-day flight-to-ferry plans.
  • Get to the airport 3 hours early for your flight home.

Our flight advice

When to book: The sweet spot for US to Greece flights in May is about 6 months out, so around December 2026. Airlines release schedules 9 to 11 months ahead, which is a good time to start tracking prices. The best fares usually show up 2 to 7 months out. That said, if you want to get your flights early, do it! It's completely up to you.

  • Look at flights first. Find prices and times you like.
  • Land in Greece by Sunday, May 9 at the latest for no stress with the ferries (you'll need a hotel the night before). Better yet, come for the weekend and see another island first.
  • For home, fly out Sunday, May 16. Saturday ferries back can land late. Flying home the same day as your ferry? Leave at least 3 to 4 hours between the ferry's arrival and your flight, since weather can delay boats.
  • Send us your flights and ferries before you book if you're unsure. We want to help.
  • Once booked, fill out the Flight + Info Form. It's also where you tell us your dietary needs, health notes and emergency contact. This is how we set your port pickup and group you with others on your ferry.

Running late or stuck?

Email us at habitat@habitatretreats.com as soon as you know. On travel day you can also text or WhatsApp Kennon (+1 512 627 2297) or Carrigan (+1 903 515 0061). We'll rework your transfer. Missed your ferry? Book the next one and tell us which. We'll get you from the port.

Ferry tips (read before you book)

  • Buy one ticket all the way through when you can. If your flights are on separate tickets and the first one is late, the second airline doesn't have to rebook you. If you do book separately, leave a big buffer.
  • Book ferries once schedules are out and save the e-ticket to your phone. The name must match your passport, and you may be asked for ID when boarding.
  • Get to the port 45 to 60 minutes early. Greek ports are busy, gates can be far apart, and boats don't wait. Piraeus is huge, so check your gate on the ticket.
  • Santorini's ferry port (Athinios) is 20 to 30 minutes below Fira on a winding road. Taxis are scarce when big boats come in, so pre-book a transfer or ask your hotel.
  • You handle your own bags on board. Big suitcases go in a luggage area near the entrance. Keep valuables and meds with you.
  • Prone to seasickness? Take something before you board and sit low and in the middle. The fast boats are bumpier.

If your ferry is delayed or cancelled

It happens, usually because of wind. The ferry company will move you to the next boat. Email us and text Kennon or Carrigan right away, and we'll move your pickup. If you're stuck overnight, stay put, get a room near the port, and keep your receipts for insurance. Unlikely any of this happens, but not impossible with travel.

Extending your trip?

There are so many Greek islands, and every one is different. If you're adding days before or after the retreat and want recommendations, or you're curious whether we have hotel picks for a certain island, email us.

Payments, cancellations + insurance

Deposit + balance

Your $500 deposit is paid and your spot is held. Your full balance is due by April 10, 2027 (30 days before the retreat), following the payment plan you chose at checkout. Payments come out automatically on the card saved at checkout and show on your statement as HABITAT RETREATS.

Late payments: Because we pay venues and vendors well in advance, every installment needs to land on time. Each one has a 5-day grace period. After that, a 3% late fee is added to the overdue amount. If you see a problem coming, tell us before the due date. We're always happy to work with you when we hear early.

Questions about your payments? Email habitat@habitatretreats.com.

Travel insurance

Strongly recommended. It covers what we can't: missed ferries, lost bags, medical care abroad, and cancelling for illness or emergencies.

  • Look for: trip cancellation + interruption, medical + evacuation, baggage delay.
  • Buy it soon after booking. Many policies only cover pre-existing conditions if you buy within 14 to 21 days of your first payment.
  • Check your credit card. Some premium cards already include trip coverage.
  • We have used BattleFace in the past. Ask ChatGPT what your credit card covers, it's a fast way to find out.
08

Passports, health + safety

Entering Europe: the short version

If you're a US citizen, you need a valid passport and some patience at passport control. No visa. No application (for now). Here's everything else.

Your passport

  • It must be valid for at least 3 months after you leave Europe and issued within the last 10 years. Greece is part of the Schengen Area, so these are the Schengen rules.
  • Our rule is stricter: valid until at least November 15, 2027. Airlines sometimes deny boarding when it's close, and it's not worth the stress.
  • Have at least one blank page.
  • Renewing? Routine US renewals take weeks, and the online renewal system is fastest. Do it this fall, not in April. Send us your new passport number when it arrives.
  • The name on your flights and ferry tickets must match your passport exactly.

Visa + the 90/180 rule

  • US citizens don't need a visa for tourist stays up to 90 days.
  • Those 90 days are counted across all Schengen countries (Greece, Italy, France, Spain and more) in any rolling 180-day window.
  • Only matters if you're spending a lot of time in Europe this year. If you are, check the EU's short-stay calculator.

EES: the new digital border check

The EU's Entry/Exit System (EES) has been fully live at every Schengen border, including all Greek airports, since April 10, 2026. It replaces passport stamps with a digital record.

What happens at passport control:

  • Get in the non-EU passports line.
  • Hand over your passport. Hats and sunglasses off.
  • They take your photo and scan 4 fingerprints (sometimes at a self-service kiosk first, then an officer).
  • You may be asked where you're staying, how long, and to show a return ticket. Have your hotel address and flight home saved on your phone.
  • Done. Your registration is saved for 3 years, so future trips are faster.

When you leave Europe, you'll go through EES again on exit (quicker, usually a face scan or fingerprint).

What this means for you:

  • Lines can be long. Travelers have reported multi-hour waits at peak times, occasionally more. Off-peak, it's about a minute per person.
  • You clear EES at your first Schengen airport. Flying Austin to Frankfurt to Athens? You'll do it in Frankfurt. Flying via London or Istanbul (not Schengen)? You'll do it in Greece.
  • Small island airports have the worst lines. Santorini and Mykonos have struggled most. If you're flying into an island, try to connect through a big Schengen hub (Athens, Frankfurt, Paris, Amsterdam, Munich, Zurich) so you clear EES there.
  • Give connections room. If you land from the US and connect in Europe, leave at least 2 hours. Airline minimums don't account for EES lines.
  • On the way home, arrive at the airport 2 hours before your flight. Athens Airport now asks non-EU travelers to arrive at least 2.5 hours early.
  • No app needed for Greece. The EU's "Travel to Europe" pre-registration app only works at a few borders and doesn't include Greece right now.

Coming home to the US

Have Global Entry? Use it. If not, the free Mobile Passport Control app can shorten your line at many US airports.

Not a US citizen?

Canadian, UK and Australian citizens also travel visa-free under the same 90/180 and EES rules. Other passports may need a Schengen visa, which takes months. Check your own government's travel advice and tell us your nationality in your Flight + Info Form so we can help.

Health

  • No vaccines are required for Greece. Make sure routine vaccines are up to date. CDC: Greece
  • Tell us about allergies, injuries, pregnancy or health conditions in your Flight + Info Form. We only share it with who needs to know (the kitchen, your leaders). Please be thorough. The more we know, the better we can look after you on a small island.
  • Bring prescriptions in original, labeled packaging with a copy of the prescription, plus a few extra days' supply in your carry-on.
  • Some common US meds are controlled in Greece, including ADHD stimulants (Adderall, Ritalin), codeine and other opioids, and benzodiazepines (Xanax, Valium). If you take any of these, bring only what you need for the trip and a signed letter from your doctor in English listing the medication, dose and why you take it. Check with your doctor or the Greek embassy if you're unsure.
  • Amorgos has small clinics and pharmacies, including one in Aegiali. Serious cases go to Naxos or Athens.
  • Drink bottled or filtered water on the islands.
  • The Greek sun is strong even in May. SPF, hat and water are a must.

Safety

Amorgos is very safe and relaxed. Normal travel sense applies.

  • Keep your passport in the room safe. Keep a digital copy of it on your phone.
  • Don't leave bags unattended in public spaces.
09

Know before you go: Greece

Weather in May

Warm, sunny days and cool evenings. May can be breezy on the islands. Pack a layer.

Amorgos, mid-MayDayNightSeaRain
TypicalAbout 22°C / 72°FAbout 16°C / 61°FAbout 18°C / 64°FRare

Time zone

Greece is 8 hours ahead of Austin and 10 hours ahead of Los Angeles in May.

Money

  • Currency: Euro (€). Check xe.com for the current rate.
  • Cards work at the hotel and most restaurants. Smaller tavernas, taxis and shops may be cash only, but historically we have been able to use card everywhere.
  • To get cash, use bank ATMs, not Euronet. When asked, always choose to pay in euros, not dollars.

Tipping

Tipping is completely up to you and your experience. It's never required, but it's appreciated by the people who make the week happen. Had an incredible experience? Tip more. Felt more "meh"? That's OK too.

  • Hotel team: When you do your room check out, you can leave gratuity for them if you would like. Tip what you'd like, and it's shared among the staff who looked after us.
  • Boat crew and hike guide: Tip them directly at the end of the activity, if you'd like.
  • Restaurants on your own: 5 to 10% for good service is normal, left in cash.
  • Taxis: Round up.

Cash (euros) is easiest for tips.

Phone + data

  • Check your carrier's international plan, or get an eSIM (Airalo or Holafly). Install at home, switch on when you land.
  • Our group message is how we'll all talk.
  • Signal on Amorgos is decent in towns and can drop on hikes and boats.

Plugs + power

Greece uses Type C and F plugs (two round pins), 230V. Bring an adapter. Phone and laptop chargers are fine. US hair tools usually aren't, so bring dual-voltage or use the hotel hairdryer.

Local customs

  • Dinner is late. 8 or 9pm is normal (but we will be eating earlier).
  • Island life is slow. Service is relaxed. Lean in.
  • Three words: Yassas (hello), Efharisto (thank you), Yamas (cheers).

What to expect on retreat

Your hosts

KENNON GOLDREYER
Co-founder, Habitat Retreats

Kennon came into Habitat already believing the best trips are the ones you can't fully explain to people back home. She's your hype girl on the ground, the one who's already scoped the best swimming spot before anyone else wakes up.

CARRIGAN WHITELEY
Co-founder, Habitat Retreats

Carrigan started Habitat because she knew there was a way to take more intentional vacations, and build a community around it at the same time. She's the one who'll talk you into the ridge hike, then hand you a glass of wine at the top.

We're with you the whole week, and we teach every class. No handoffs.

Classes

  • Reformer Pilates most mornings, yoga at golden hour on some evenings.
  • All levels. Options for first-timers and challenges for regulars.
  • Always optional. Sometimes the moments you follow your intuition on a retreat become the most memorable.
  • Injured, pregnant, or recovering? Tell us in your Flight + Info Form and before class.
  • Reformers, mats and props provided. Grip socks required on the reformer.

Food

  • Breakfast and dinner are included every day. Breakfast is after Pilates, and dinner is at Aegialis or with the group at tavernas in town. Lunch is on the boat on Wednesday. Other days, midday is yours: most people grab food by the pool (charged to your room), lunch in town, or something at a beach bar.
  • Food at the hotel is served buffet style, with options for every diet. Vegan, vegetarian, gluten-free and allergies all covered. If something doesn't look right for you, tell us or your server. We'll fix it.
  • Want a snack between meals? Order anything and charge it to your room.

Spa + your massage

The spa is yours all week: hammam, seawater pool, jacuzzi, sauna. Your 30-min massage is included. Book with spa reception or the hotel front desk, or email spa@aegialis.com. We'll go over the schedule on day 1 so you can book it in free time. Want 60 minutes? Upgrade at the spa.

Free time

Real free time is built in, on purpose. Pool, spa, nap, beach, a walk into Aegiali for frozen yogurt or a freddo espresso. We'll share our favorite spots in the chat.

Staying in touch

  • Email: the best way to reach us about anything before the retreat starts, plus payments, forms and this guide.
  • Group message: There will be a retreat group chat made for communication right before and during the retreat. It's where we post daily updates and generally communicate during the week. Heads up: your name and number will be visible to everyone in it.
  • Ferry group chats: About a week out, we group you with everyone on your ferry so you can find each other and ride to the hotel together.
  • Group call: About a month before the retreat, 30 min. We'll send the date and time closer to it. Meet everyone and ask anything. Notes sent after if you can't make it.

Anonymous feedback

We want this to be your best week. We also know it's hard to tell the hosts something isn't working. So during the retreat, an anonymous form stays open and we check it every day. Wishing there was more of something? Room issue? Someone making you uncomfortable? Tell us early so we can fix it before you go home. Anonymous Feedback Form

Arrival + check-out day

  • Check-in: Bring your passport. Greek hotels are required to see it at check-in.
  • Arriving early? If your room isn't ready, the hotel will store your bags and you can head to the pool or spa.
  • Check-out day: Rooms are out by 11am. The hotel will hold your bags until your port transfer, and you're welcome to use the spa and hang around the property until then.

If you get sick or hurt

Tell us right away, day or night. We'll help you get to the pharmacy in Aegiali or the local clinic, and contact your insurer with you if needed. Serious cases are transferred to Naxos or Athens, which is why travel insurance with medical evacuation matters.

Valuables

Leave expensive jewelry at home. Keep your passport, cards and cash in the room safe. Habitat isn't responsible for lost or damaged belongings, so bring nothing you'd be heartbroken to lose.

Extras

  • Room tab: Extras (snacks, drinks, laundry, extra spa) go on your room bill. Settle it at check-out before departing.
  • Laundry: Bags in your room. Charged to your tab.
  • Photos: Lots of photos get taken by everyone during the week. We make it easy to share them with a group photo album. More on that during the week.
  • Waiver: Your liability waiver is attached to the email with this guide. Fill it out, sign it and email it back to habitat@habitatretreats.com before May 10. You can't take part without it.
  • Be on time for transfers and excursions. Anything you book on your own during free time (scooter rentals, extra tours) isn't run by Habitat and is at your own risk.

After the retreat

  • Photos: We'll share a group album with photos from the week.
  • Feedback survey: You'll get a short, fully anonymous survey after the trip. We rely on it heavily to make every retreat better, so please be honest.
  • Left something behind? Tell the hotel directly and we'll help where we can.
11

Packing list

Luggage: Completely up to you how much you bring. This is your vacation! If you have tight connections or multiple separate bookings, carry-on luggage may be best. Put your name and number on everything in case it gets lost.

Pack a carry-on like your checked bag might be late. If you're checking a bag, pack a swimsuit, one workout set, grip socks, a change of clothes, meds, chargers and toiletries for 2 days, just in case.

Travel essentials

  • Passport (valid until Nov 15, 2027) + a photo of it
  • Phone, charger, power bank
  • Type C/F plug adapters
  • Debit card in case you want to visit the ATM for cash
  • Travel insurance details, return flight and hotel address saved offline (border officers may ask)
  • Prescription meds in original packaging + prescription copy (and a doctor's letter for controlled meds)
  • Headphones, eye mask, earplugs
  • Reusable water bottle
  • Motion sickness tablets or bands (ferries + boat day)

Movement (1 to 2 classes a day)

  • Athletic/workout clothes (re-wearing is totally fine, no need for one set per class)
  • Grip socks for the reformer
  • Sneakers for the hike

Evenings

  • Dinner outfits. Whatever you want to wear on vacation, this is your week.
  • Light sweater or wrap. It gets breezy.

Days

  • Swimsuits + a cover-up
  • Sandals + comfortable walking shoes (hills + steps)
  • Hat + sunglasses
  • Sunscreen
  • Beach bag or tote, plus water shoes (rocky beaches and sea urchins)
  • Something that covers shoulders and knees for the monastery

Toiletries + health

  • Any toiletries you're picky about (the hotel provides the basics and a hair dryer)
  • After-sun or aloe
  • Basic meds: pain reliever, antihistamine, stomach settler, blister plasters

Nice to have

  • A good book for the pool
  • A deck of cards

Leave at home

  • US hair tools that aren't dual-voltage
  • Your yoga mat (we have them)
  • Towels (the hotel has them)

13

FAQ

Before you go

I'm coming alone. Will that be weird?
Not even a little.

I've never done reformer Pilates. Is that OK?
Yes. Every class is all levels and optional, and you'll get options for your body. Let us know if you want some extra instruction outside of class.

Can I bring a friend?
Absolutely! Tell them to book the same way you did and we'll room you together.

How old are people who come?
This group usually ranges from about 28 to 65, but every age is welcome. The common thread is curiosity, not age.

Can I change my room type?
If a private room is available, of course. Ask and we'll make it happen.

Can I give my spot to a friend?
If you need to cancel, any balance we keep under the cancellation policy can go toward a friend who takes your spot. Your deposit can't be transferred. Email us and we'll set it up.

What's the pace like?
Slower, on purpose. Reformer and yoga, long meals, and open afternoons. Not high adrenaline.

Travel

Why isn't there a flight to Amorgos?
There's no airport. That's why it's not over-touristed. You fly, then ferry.

Which gateway should I pick?
Santorini for the shortest ferry and a pretty night. Naxos for calm and value. Athens if flights are much cheaper and you don't mind a long ferry.

When will ferry tickets be available?
Usually early in the year. We'll send times and links as soon as they're out.

What if my flight or ferry is delayed?
Email us right away. On travel day, text Kennon or Carrigan. We'll help you as best we can and rework your pickup.

On retreat

How hard is the hike?
Not long, and very doable. It's 6.1 km (3.8 miles) with 138 m (450 ft) of elevation gain, and takes 2 to 3 hours depending on your pace. It's one way, not a loop, so no doubling back. Wear sneakers, bring water and a hat, and go at your own speed.

Do I have to do everything?
No. Every class and activity is optional.

How much free time is there?
Plenty. Tuesday and Thursday are mostly free after morning Pilates, apart from a yoga class and dinner. Wednesday is the boat, and Friday morning is the hike.

I have a food allergy. Will I be OK?
Yes. Put it in your Flight + Info Form. The kitchen will know your name and your allergy.

Are meals included?
Breakfast and dinner every day, including every dinner in town. Lunch is included on boat day. Otherwise midday is free, and most people eat by the pool, in town, or at a beach bar.

Is alcohol included?
The wine tasting and drinks on boat day are. Other drinks go on your room tab.

What if I don't click with my roommate?
Tell us privately or through the Anonymous Feedback Form. We'll handle it quietly.

What should I wear to dinner?
Whatever you'd wear on vacation. Nothing formal.

Money

Should I tip?
See Tipping in Know Before You Go.
